text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- The editorial urges all political parties to participate in elections if they want to see Albania emerge from crisis.
- The newspaper publishes documents it alleges show that northern Albanians were organised by President Sali Berisha's administration to crack down on demonstrators in the south.

- While Prime Minister Bashkim Fino shook hands with U.S. President Bill Clinton in Hague, President Sali Berisha visited villages around Tirana trying to convince farmers to vote for his Democratic Party.
- The OSCE wants to have three representatives in the Central Election Commission.
- Leaders of the so-called committee of public salvation in Sarande warned President Sali Berisha not to visit their town, saying he is widely blamed for the violence and chaos.
- Gramsh residents are armed to the teeth and their houses turned into real fortifications after they looted Albania's main military depot.
ALBANIA
- We opposed a national reconciliation formula to the communist armed rebellion, President Sali Berisha told a German parliamentary delegation.
- Albanians, having been cheated by a communist dictatorship for half a century, should only vote for rightist parties.
- The Democratic Party hailed U.S. disapproval of any possible election boycott by the leftist parties.
- Unknown people opened fire at the residence of Sylva investment company boss Pellum Shehaj. No casualties were reported.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The Socialist Party agreed to back candidates from the Social Democratic Party and Democratic Alliance Party in some electoral zones.
- Albania's United Right, an alliance of six rightist parties, vowed to oust President Sali Berisha's Democrats and prevent the ex-communists from returning to power.

- Hospital workers in the southern town of Fier threatened they would resign if police failed to secure the hospital from attacks. They also protested at the local authority's failure to pay them monthly wages and promised recompenses.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Berisha said so-called committees of public salvation in the south should be disbanded ahead of elections.
- The newspaper carries a report on violence across the country. Tens of people have been killed or injured over past days.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano is visiting Italy on the invitation of the Italian Social Democratic Party. He will also have talks with Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

- President Sali Berisha's administration wanted to sell Albanian property for political interests, the newspaper alleges. It published a document it said was signed by former Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi, handing the country's main chrome mines to Germany's Preussag Anlangenbau for only $ 3.5 millions.
